title: Florida Learjet 60 Crash: The Last 4 Minutes — What the NTSB Has Said So Far
desc:
The Florida Learjet 60 crash (Nov 1, 2026, Greenacres / Palm Beach County), explained only with what the NTSB and the FAA have said so far: the radio calls as NTSB investigators described them, the weather questions, the wreckage, the left elevator found miles away, and the cockpit voice recorder.

At about 12:47 p.m. EST, at 35,000 ft, the crew reported light clear ice, moderate turbulence and altitude deviations of about 700 ft, and asked to climb to 37,000 ft. Less than 30 seconds later, according to the NTSB, a transmission announced the descent, followed by a mayday call. Impact was at about 12:51 p.m. All nine people on board were killed. This is a breakdown of the official record so far — not a finding of cause. The NTSB has not determined a probable cause.
